items.q: The Maltese cross seen in the kidney on polarizing microscopy is listed for all of the following EXCEPT:
opts: Nephrotic syndrome
Fabry's disease
ADPKD
Prerenal azotemia
items.exp: The 'In kidney' list is Fabry's disease, ADPKD, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis and prerenal azotemia; lipiduria of nephrotic syndrome produces oval fat bodies but is not one of the printed kidney causes on this page. (Book p745)

items.q: The same Maltese-cross appearance is attributed in blood to babesiosis.
opts: True — 'In blood: Babesiosis' is the first bullet under the polarizing microscope line
False — in blood the Maltese cross marks malaria pigment
False — the blood bullet lists oval fat bodies instead
True — and the same bullet list also includes ADPKD under blood
items.exp: Polarizing microscope: maltese cross appearance — In blood: babesiosis; In kidney: Fabry's disease, ADPKD, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis, prerenal azotemia. (Book p745)

items.q: A patient with polycystic kidneys has urine microscopy performed under polarized light and the technologist reports Maltese-cross bodies. Reading this page, the correct interpretation is:
opts: A recognised renal cause of the Maltese cross, alongside Fabry's disease and interstitial nephritis
Proof of concurrent babesiosis
An artefact, since Maltese crosses appear only in blood
Evidence of prerenal azotemia alone
items.exp: ADPKD is one of the four listed renal causes of a Maltese cross on polarizing microscopy, so the finding fits the underlying cystic disease rather than an artefact or a blood parasite. (Book p745)

items.q: The caption printed beneath the first pair of photographs on this page reads:
opts: Phase contrast microscopy with monomorphic red cells
Polarized oval fat bodies with maltese cross
Tubular epithelial cell with nucleus
Granular cytoplasm & lobulated nucleus
items.exp: The caption under the large orange field (with the arrow to a large white cell) is 'Phase contrast microscopy with monomorphic red cells'; the other three captions sit on the remaining figures of the page. (Book p745)

items.q: In this page's cast table, 'Coarse granular cast' is printed as a row label without its own clinical-association cell.
opts: True — only the hyaline and fine granular rows carry condition cells on this page
False — coarse granular casts are marked 'Kidney disease' in a separate cell
False — the coarse granular row is marked 'Normal'
True — and the same is true of the hyaline cast row
items.exp: The table on p745 shows a hyaline-cast photo against 'Normal, Kidney disease', then a bare 'Coarse granular cast' label, then the fine granular photo against 'Kidney disease'. (Book p745)
